overview: Edison International is a holding company whose principal subsidiary, Southern California Edison (SCE), is a vertically integrated, rate-regulated electric utility serving about 15 million people across a roughly 50,000-square-mile service territory in central, coastal and Southern California. SCE generates, transmits and distributes electricity to residential, commercial, industrial and public-sector customers under rates set by the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) and the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC). The company's earnings and growth are driven almost entirely by SCE's regulated rate base, offset by substantial exposure to California wildfire liability.

business_model.summary: EIX earns a CPUC/FERC-authorized return on SCE's regulated asset (rate) base. Revenue is collected through cost-of-service rates set in periodic General Rate Cases (GRC, typically 4-year cycles) and formula transmission rates at FERC, with balancing accounts that true up actual costs (including wildfire mitigation, fuel and purchased power) against rates collected. Growth comes from capital investment in grid hardening, reliability, transmission and distribution infrastructure and electrification-enabling upgrades, which expands the rate base on which SCE earns its allowed ROE (~10.1-10.6% range in recent GRC decisions). Virtually all cash flow is recurring and regulator-sanctioned rather than transactional or market-based.
business_model.customer_type: Regulated B2C and B2B/public-sector electric utility customers (residential, commercial, industrial, agricultural, public authorities) within SCE's franchised service territory; no retail choice/competition for bundled distribution service
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% California (SCE service territory: parts of Los Angeles, Orange, San Bernardino, Riverside, Kern, Fresno, Inyo, Kings, Mono, Santa Barbara, Tulare and Ventura counties)

main_competitors: PG&E and SDG&E as peer CA IOUs for regulatory/legislative comparisons
Municipal utilities (e.g., LADWP) at service-territory boundaries
Community Choice Aggregators (CCAs) for generation procurement
Behind-the-meter solar/storage providers as a disintermediation threat
competitive_position.market_position: SCE is the second-largest electric utility in California by customers (after PG&E) and operates as a legally franchised monopoly for transmission and distribution service in its territory; it does not compete for bundled delivery customers but does face erosion of generation-procurement revenue to CCAs and distributed solar/storage.

moat_factors.description: Exclusive right to provide transmission/distribution service in its territory under CPUC and FERC jurisdiction; essential-service demand is highly inelastic
CPUC rate-case mechanics and FERC formula rates provide a contractual-like, cost-of-service return on invested capital, supporting predictable long-term earnings growth tied to capex
Extensive existing transmission/distribution network and interconnection infrastructure represent a high replication barrier
State-sponsored $21B wildfire insurance fund (shared across PG&E, SCE, SDG&E) absorbs a portion of catastrophic wildfire liability for prudently-operated utilities, partially mitigating tail risk

weaknesses: No diversification outside California; fully exposed to one state's regulatory and political environment
Wildfire liability risk is severity-unbounded relative to the shared state fund's finite capacity
CCA migration and rooftop solar/NEM erode the generation-procurement portion of the revenue base
Regulatory lag and politically contentious rate cases can delay cost recovery and depress near-term ROE realization
High and rising customer bills create political pressure that can slow capex approvals or compress allowed returns

growth_drivers: SCE rate base growth of roughly 7% CAGR (2025-2030) driven by grid hardening, wildfire mitigation, transmission and distribution capital programs
~$38-41 billion five-year (2026-2030) capital investment plan, including a targeted ~$9 billion annual capital deployment pace entering the next GRC cycle
Grid modernization / AMI 2.0 (advanced metering) deployment expected to support accelerated rate base growth after 2028
Electrification of transportation and buildings in California increasing system load and incremental distribution investment needs
Clean energy policy tailwinds (state decarbonization mandates, transmission buildout for renewables interconnection)
Management's reaffirmed long-term target of 5-7% core EPS growth through 2030, with financing plan that does not currently assume new common equity issuance through 2030

business.risk: Wildfire ignition and liability from SCE equipment
business.description: LA County Fire Dept/CAL FIRE investigators (August 2026) attributed the January 2025 Eaton Fire, which killed 19 people and destroyed/damaged more than 9,000 structures, to electrical arcing on an idle SCE transmission tower; thousands of lawsuits are pending and causation/prudency findings are still being litigated

California's inverse-condemnation doctrine can impose strict liability on utilities for wildfire property damage caused by their equipment regardless of fault/negligence, a structurally adverse legal regime unique to the state
Community Choice Aggregators and behind-the-meter solar/storage reduce the generation-procurement revenue SCE handles, though distribution/transmission rate base is less affected
Rising customer bills from wildfire mitigation and capex recovery create political risk to future rate case outcomes

financial.risk: Balance sheet strain from wildfire claims
financial.description: Potential multi-billion-dollar Eaton Fire liabilities, securitization of wildfire costs, and elevated leverage; Fitch moved its outlook on EIX/SCE to negative from stable in September 2026 citing the stalled legislative reform push
Large capital program and litigation costs could eventually force new equity issuance (not currently planned through 2030) or higher-cost debt if credit metrics deteriorate further

financial.risk: Depletion of the AB 1054 wildfire insurance fund
financial.description: State officials have warned the Eaton Fire claims alone could exhaust a meaningful share of the ~$21B statewide fund, reducing the backstop available for future events and raising replenishment/assessment risk for utility shareholders and ratepayers

regulatory.risk: Failure of wildfire liability reform legislation
regulatory.description: SB 492, a 2026 legislative deal to raise prudency standards and limit certain claims, collapsed in the Assembly (September 1, 2026) after opposition from fire survivors, consumer groups and insufficient relief for utilities; no durable reform is currently in place and the stock fell ~24% on the news

regulatory.risk: CPUC rate case / cost disallowance risk
regulatory.description: GRC and wildfire-mitigation cost recovery requests can be reduced or delayed, and prudency reviews could find SCE's conduct unreasonable, triggering fund repayment obligations (reported cap figures of ~$3.9-4.0B cited in press coverage)

regulatory.risk: Potential new legislative session / special session
regulatory.description: Lawmakers have signaled fall 2026 hearings and a possible special session on wildfire liability reform; outcome and timing remain uncertain

macro.description: As a capital-intensive, debt-funded utility, EIX's financing costs and valuation are sensitive to long-term interest rate levels

macro.risk: Wildfire frequency/severity tied to climate and drought conditions
macro.description: Hotter, drier conditions and Santa Ana wind events increase both the probability and severity of utility-equipment-caused wildfires across SCE's territory
Wildfire losses have reduced the availability and raised the cost of third-party liability insurance for California utilities

macro_factors.industry_outlook: US regulated electric utilities face above-trend rate base growth from grid hardening, electrification and data-center/AI-driven load growth; California utilities specifically face elevated wildfire liability risk that differentiates them from the broader sector
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low - regulated utility demand is largely non-discretionary, though wildfire litigation and legislative outcomes introduce large, event-driven swings in equity value
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-to-high - utility sector valuations and financing costs move inversely with long-term rates; EIX's wildfire-related financing needs amplify this sensitivity

recent_developments.event: LA County Fire Department and CAL FIRE investigators concluded electrical arcing on an idle SCE transmission tower in Eaton Canyon started the January 2025 Eaton Fire, which killed 19 people and destroyed or damaged over 9,000 structures; SCE said it is reviewing the report
California's SB 492 wildfire liability reform deal, negotiated with Gov. Newsom, collapsed when the Assembly declined to vote on it; EIX shares fell roughly 24% intraday on the news

Fitch Ratings revised its outlook on Edison International and SCE to negative from stable, citing the stalled wildfire liability reform effort; several sell-side analysts (Jefferies, Truist) cut price targets
California Legislature adjourned its session without passing wildfire liability reform; lawmakers signaled fall hearings and a possible special session

Q3 2026 results: core EPS $1.92 (GAAP $1.88) vs. $2.34 core in Q3 2025 (which had benefited from a GRC decision one-time boost); beat consensus (~$1.81-1.83) on EPS but revenue of ~$4.89B missed estimates; full-year 2026 core EPS guidance reaffirmed at $5.90-$6.20

Edison and the other two major California IOUs told state wildfire-fund authority officials that utility shareholders should not be required to contribute additional capital to the AB 1054 wildfire fund, arguing it would undermine investor confidence in California utilities

items.notes: Reaffirmed at Q3 2026; basic (GAAP) EPS guidance range of $5.66-$5.96, down slightly from $5.70-$6.00 issued in July 2026, reflecting ~$0.24/share of non-core items
Longer-term core EPS guidance cited at $6.25-$6.65 for 2027 and $6.74-$7.14 for 2028 in recent investor materials
Driven by grid hardening, wildfire mitigation and T&D capital programs; potential acceleration post-2028 tied to AMI 2.0 and next GRC cycle
Implies a targeted ~$9 billion annual capital deployment pace entering the next General Rate Case cycle

items.target: No new common equity issuance assumed
items.notes: Management has stated the current financing plan relies on operating cash flow and debt rather than new equity, though this is contingent on wildfire liability outcomes

guidance.management_commentary: Management reaffirmed full-year 2026 core EPS guidance despite the Q3 revenue miss and continues to frame durable wildfire liability reform as a top priority, warning that further delays in legislative reform are a risk to the cost of capital and pace of grid investment. Executives have emphasized that SCE held a valid wildfire safety certification at the time of the Eaton Fire, which creates a rebuttable presumption of prudent operation under AB 1054, and that losses above $1.0 billion for third-party Eaton Fire damages are expected to be reimbursable from the state Wildfire Insurance Fund, subject to fund administrator approval and the fund's claims-paying capacity.

bull_case: Regulated monopoly utility with highly predictable, rate-base-driven earnings growth (5-7% core EPS CAGR target) and a large, visible $38-41B five-year capital program
AB 1054 wildfire fund and the prudent-operator safety-certification presumption provide a meaningful (if imperfect and contested) backstop against catastrophic Eaton Fire liability
Secular tailwinds from California electrification, grid hardening mandates and clean energy policy support above-average rate base growth versus typical US utilities

Valuation has compressed sharply (shares down ~24% on the SB 492 collapse, trading well below prior-year price targets), offering recovery upside if wildfire liability reform ultimately passes or litigation outcomes are more favorable than feared
Company maintains it can fund its capital plan through 2030 without issuing new common equity, limiting near-term dilution risk
bear_case: Eaton Fire causation findings (SCE equipment implicated by LA County Fire/CAL FIRE) expose the company to potentially multi-billion-dollar liabilities from thousands of pending lawsuits, with outcome highly dependent on contested prudency determinations

California's wildfire liability reform (SB 492) collapsed in September 2026 with no replacement yet enacted, leaving the regulatory/legal backstop for utility wildfire risk structurally unresolved and a recurring source of headline risk each legislative session

The $21B AB 1054 wildfire fund may be substantially depleted by Eaton Fire claims alone, reducing the cushion available for future wildfire events and raising the risk of additional utility/ratepayer contributions
Negative rating action (Fitch outlook cut to negative) and declining analyst price targets (several cuts into the $53-$70 range) signal deteriorating credit and equity sentiment

100% California concentration leaves EIX fully exposed to one state's wildfire risk, inverse-condemnation legal doctrine, and politically volatile legislative/regulatory process, with limited diversification to offset any adverse outcome
